bull_bear.body:
- Multi-shore manufacturing across India and the UAE lets the Company redirect production and export flows between plants in response to trade-policy shocks, with the Dubai facility providing meaningful potential tariff advantages in the context of the evolving U.S. trade environment
- Exclusive licensing rights from SQIP, LLC to manufacture Marquartz, a patented engineered quartz product, across the MENA region with a First Right of Refusal for India, backed by over 20 utility patents secured across the platform in the past seven years plus proprietary RIFT VEIN and CONVERGENCE technologies
- Early mover in engineered quartz surfaces with less than 1% crystalline silica content using premium Cristobalite, a proactive response to tightening global regulation on respirable crystalline silica following measures such as Australia's 2024 prohibition
- Location advantages: SEZ status in Jaipur and Free Trade Zone status in Dubai give tax incentives, simplified regulatory processes and export competitiveness, with proximity to Jebel Ali Port enabling faster delivery and lower freight costs
- Advanced process technology base including CNC automation, rubber-mould press technology and Italian BRETON and German KEDA machinery, plus SAP ERP and a phased barcode-based inventory tracking rollout
- In-house Research & Development centre at the SEZ unit driving new design development, process optimisation and quality enhancement
- Reference credentials in premium projects including Dubai Mall and Emaar St. Regis, alongside new developer relationships with Damac and Sobha in the Middle East
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- US trade-policy and tariff exposure on India-origin quartz exports — Management describes tariff-related uncertainty in the US as, without question, the single most significant external factor affecting performance during the year, particularly in the second half: it compressed realisations, introduced hesitancy into customer ordering patterns and contributed meaningfully to fourth-quarter margin pressure. India segment revenue fell to `748.36 million from `1,419.12 million and the USA segment to `523.43 million from `831.41 million, both attributed to elevated tariffs and evolving trade-policy uncertainty.
- Pending QMAA Section 201 global safeguard petition in the United States — Foreign-manufactured quartz surface products currently represent approximately 90% of the U.S. market, which led the QMAA to file the Section 201 safeguard petition. The Board's Report calls the potential imposition of a broad-based global safeguard tariff a watershed development for all quartz-exporting nations including India — an unresolved regulatory event that could reset access to the Company's largest market.
- Extreme geographic and single-market revenue concentration — The USA alone accounted for 77.2% of FY26 revenue and North America (USA and Canada combined) 82.2% of total revenue. Diversification is under way — North America's share fell from an implied 88.8% in FY25 while MENA rose from 7.9% to 13.2% — but the business remains dependent on one policy jurisdiction, and the Company is explicit that it moved deliberately to reduce dependence on any single market.
- Geopolitical disruption in the Middle East and Red Sea region — The Board's Report attributes part of the UAE segment loss to geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East and Red Sea region affecting logistics and demand, and the Chairman records approximately 45 days of disruption caused by the regional conflict. This is a direct threat to the shipping routes on which the Jebel Ali-based manufacturing and distribution strategy depends.
- Prolonged under-utilisation of installed capacity at both manufacturing units — The Dubai (FZE) facility averaged 44% utilisation for the full year against installed capacity of 622,895 sqm per annum, while the Jaipur SEZ unit operated at only 23% average capacity utilisation against installed capacity of 521,450 sqm per annum, reflecting broader demand softness. The UAE segment loss of `(391.76) million is attributed primarily to absorbing full depreciation and finance costs during the ongoing ramp-up and stabilisation phase, so consolidated profitability hinges on utilisation recovering.
- Loss-making consolidated operations with widening losses and negative EBITDA — The Group recorded a consolidated net loss before tax of `(230.02) million and a net loss after tax of `(318.39) million in FY26, wider than FY25's `(289.00) million, while EBITDA turned negative to INR (113) million from a positive INR 20 million and fourth-quarter EBITDA margin fell to (41.85)%. Consolidated total comprehensive loss was `(328.27) million.
- Execution risk on the Bagru unit closure and its still-unplanned disposal — The auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to the Board-approved discontinuation of the Bagru Unit (natural stone processing) with effect from March 31, 2026 in view of sustained losses and continued capacity under-utilization, noting that the Board has only accorded in-principle approval for preparation of a plan for disposal of the said unit — the disposal itself is neither planned in detail nor executed.
- Pending regulatory approval for the FZE loan-to-equity conversion — The auditor's Emphasis of Matter records that the approved conversion of an existing unsecured loan aggregating Rs. 100 Crores / USD 11,120,997 / AED 40,842,200 granted to wholly owned foreign subsidiary Global Surfaces FZE into equity shares on March 18, 2026 remained pending as at March 31, 2026, awaiting requisite approvals/formalities with the Jebel Ali Free Zone Authority (JAFZA), Dubai.
- Standalone profitability dependent on intra-group income rather than trading operations — Standalone total income of `1,122.29 million for FY26 included other income of `373.93 million, described as principally attributable to management fees, foreign exchange gains and reimbursements received from subsidiaries as part of intra-group arrangements integral to the multi-shore operating model — while those same subsidiaries were loss-making. The India segment result is likewise credited to a higher contribution from other income including intra-group management fees and reimbursements, a quality-of-earnings and related-party dependency risk.
- Deteriorating demand in the core export end-market despite intact long-term structural drivers — The Board's Report states that while structural demand drivers — construction activity, home renovation trends and increasing preference for durable, low-maintenance surfaces — remain broadly intact, the near-term environment for Indian quartz exporters has been significantly impacted by evolving trade policies in the United States, and the Chairman notes that softening global trade growth restrained capital expenditure planning across a wide range of industries, including ours.

business.body: The Company mines, processes, manufactures and supplies premium surface solutions, including engineered quartz, granite, marble and soft quartzite, in slabs and customized countertop applications. It sells largely to international markets serving residential, commercial, hospitality and institutional construction, architecture and interior design projects. Distribution in North America runs through wholly owned subsidiaries Global Surfaces Inc. and Superior Surfaces Inc., while manufacturing and MENA/Europe/Africa distribution is anchored by the wholly owned Dubai subsidiary Global Surfaces FZE.

outlook.body:
- Dual-shore / multi-shore manufacturing across the Jaipur SEZ unit and the Dubai (FZE) facility, used deliberately to reroute production and export flows in response to tariff and trade-policy shocks and to mitigate region-specific risk
- Reduce dependence on any single market by diversifying geographically: North America's revenue share fell from an implied 88.8% in FY25 to 82.2% in FY26 while MENA rose from 7.9% to 13.2%, Canada from 0.11% to 5.0% and India's domestic contribution from 3.25% to 4.6%
- Pivot the India business to a focused, engineered quartz-led operation by discontinuing the loss-making Bagru natural stone processing unit effective March 31, 2026, entering FY 2026-27 as a leaner manufacturer with a sharpened emphasis on high-value engineered quartz products
- Differentiate through proprietary product technology - Marquartz under an exclusive licence from SQIP, LLC covering MENA with First Right of Refusal in India, patented Non-Push-Up Vein and Push-Up Vein Technology plus proprietary RIFT VEIN and CONVERGENCE technologies, and over 20 utility patents secured across the platform in the past seven years
- Lead on low-silica product safety by developing engineered quartz surfaces with less than 1% crystalline silica content using premium Cristobalite, positioned as a proactive response to tightening global regulation on respirable crystalline silica
- Technology-led manufacturing: sustained investment in automation and digitalisation including CNC automation, rubber-mould press technology, Italian BRETON and German KEDA machinery, SAP ERP and a phased barcode-based inventory tracking rollout
- Cost and working-capital discipline as an explicit management priority - reduced slab thickness, new testing protocols, pre-scheduled production planning, Cristobalite sourcing strategy, and a working capital day reduction from 157 to 71
- Fund working capital growth with short-term borrowings while continuing to reduce long-term leverage
- Strengthen subsidiary capital structure, evidenced by the loan-to-equity conversion at Global Surfaces FZE
- Deepen premium, specification-led project positioning with developers and architects, building on acceptance in projects such as Dubai Mall and Emaar St. Regis and relationships with Damac and Sobha
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Global Surfaces operates two strategically located manufacturing units with a combined installed manufacturing capacity of over 11.44 lakh sq. metres per annum. The domestic SEZ unit at Mahindra World City SEZ, Sanganer, Jaipur, spread across 24,139 sq. metres, is the Company's second manufacturing facility, focuses exclusively on engineered stone manufacturing, has an installed capacity of 5,21,454 sq. metres per annum and houses an in-house Research & Development centre; in FY26 it operated at 23% average capacity utilisation against installed capacity of 521,450 sqm per annum. The international unit is operated by wholly owned subsidiary Global Surfaces FZE at Jebel Ali Free Zone, Dubai: spread across 39,657.63 sq. metres (leased), it has an installed capacity of 6,22,895 sq. metres per annum, is dedicated to engineered stone surfaces, commenced commercial production in February 2024 and completed its second full year of commercial operations in FY 2025-26. Capacity utilisation at FZE rose to a 44% average for the year, peaking at 66% in November 2025, up from single digits at commissioning within a span of 18 months, and the segment became the largest revenue contributor in the Group; the UAE segment nevertheless recorded a loss attributed primarily to continued absorption of full depreciation and finance costs on the new facility during the ongoing ramp-up and stabilisation phase. Earlier milestones were entry into natural stone processing at the Bagru unit in 2004, backward integration into quarrying through Global Mining in 2011 and the foundation and commissioning of Unit II (SEZ) in 2017-2018. On the contraction side, after evaluation by the Audit Committee the Board approved at its meeting held on February 3, 2026 the discontinuation of operations at the Company's Natural Stone Processing Unit at Bagru, Jaipur, effective from March 31, 2026, driven by sustained financial losses, cash losses and significant under-utilisation of installed capacity; with that cessation the India segment is now a focused, engineered quartz-led operation and the Company enters FY 2026-27 as a leaner, more focused manufacturer with a sharpened strategic emphasis on high-value engineered quartz products. This bundle discloses no new plant, line or capacity-addition project, and no commissioning or completion timeline for any future project; the Company's stated expansion narrative is the ramp-up of already-commissioned capacity plus restructuring initiatives and investments in product innovation and subsidiary capitalisation that are expected to lay the foundation for improved financial performance.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The global engineered quartz industry, estimated at US$14.83 billion in 2025, is expected to reach US$28.07 billion by 2034 at a CAGR of 7.2%
- The Indian engineered quartz market, valued at approximately US$889.6 million in 2025, is expected to outpace the global rate, growing at 7.6% to reach US$1,579.6 million by 2033
- India's countertop industry, valued at USD 12,846.9 million in 2025, is projected to nearly double to USD 25,071.0 million by 2033, growing at 8.7% annually, driven by urbanisation, organised housing growth and a consumer shift towards branded, premium surfacing solutions
- The global quartz market was valued at approximately USD 8.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 12.7 billion by 2034 at a CAGR of approximately 4.7%, with structural demand drivers - construction activity, home renovation trends and increasing preference for durable, low-maintenance surfaces - remaining broadly intact
- US tariff uncertainty is management's single most significant external factor: it compressed realisations, introduced hesitancy into customer ordering patterns and contributed meaningfully to fourth-quarter margin pressure; the USA accounted for 77.2% of FY26 revenue
- Foreign-manufactured quartz surface products represent approximately 90% of the U.S. market, prompting the QMAA Section 201 safeguard petition; a broad-based global safeguard tariff would be a watershed development for all quartz-exporting nations including India
- Geopolitical disruption in the Middle East and Red Sea region affected logistics and demand, including roughly 45 days of disruption at the Dubai facility
- Operating leverage lever: the Dubai facility ran at 44% average utilisation for the year with a 66% peak in November 2025 against installed capacity of 622,895 sqm p.a., while the Jaipur SEZ unit averaged 23% against 521,450 sqm p.a. - management expects improved utilisation to drive performance
- The UAE segment loss is attributed primarily to continued absorption of full depreciation and finance costs on the new facility during the ongoing ramp-up and stabilisation phase
- Mix shift toward engineered stones, now 94.3% of revenue, which grew from INR 1,950 million to INR 2,200 million, with natural stones consciously wound down
- India's domestic economy offered a comparatively stable and strengthening base, underpinned by logistics upgrades, digital infrastructure expansion, urbanisation and a shift towards higher-value manufacturing

currentContext.expansion: Global Surfaces operates two strategically located manufacturing units with a combined installed manufacturing capacity of over 11.44 lakh sq. metres per annum. The domestic SEZ unit at Mahindra World City SEZ, Sanganer, Jaipur, spread across 24,139 sq. metres, is the Company's second manufacturing facility, focuses exclusively on engineered stone manufacturing, has an installed capacity of 5,21,454 sq. metres per annum and houses an in-house Research & Development centre; in FY26 it operated at 23% average capacity utilisation against installed capacity of 521,450 sqm per annum. The international unit is operated by wholly owned subsidiary Global Surfaces FZE at Jebel Ali Free Zone, Dubai: spread across 39,657.63 sq. metres (leased), it has an installed capacity of 6,22,895 sq. metres per annum, is dedicated to engineered stone surfaces, commenced commercial production in February 2024 and completed its second full year of commercial operations in FY 2025-26. Capacity utilisation at FZE rose to a 44% average for the year, peaking at 66% in November 2025, up from single digits at commissioning within a span of 18 months, and the segment became the largest revenue contributor in the Group; the UAE segment nevertheless recorded a loss attributed primarily to continued absorption of full depreciation and finance costs on the new facility during the ongoing ramp-up and stabilisation phase. Earlier milestones were entry into natural stone processing at the Bagru unit in 2004, backward integration into quarrying through Global Mining in 2011 and the foundation and commissioning of Unit II (SEZ) in 2017-2018. On the contraction side, after evaluation by the Audit Committee the Board approved at its meeting held on February 3, 2026 the discontinuation of operations at the Company's Natural Stone Processing Unit at Bagru, Jaipur, effective from March 31, 2026, driven by sustained financial losses, cash losses and significant under-utilisation of installed capacity; with that cessation the India segment is now a focused, engineered quartz-led operation and the Company enters FY 2026-27 as a leaner, more focused manufacturer with a sharpened strategic emphasis on high-value engineered quartz products. This bundle discloses no new plant, line or capacity-addition project, and no commissioning or completion timeline for any future project; the Company's stated expansion narrative is the ramp-up of already-commissioned capacity plus restructuring initiatives and investments in product innovation and subsidiary capitalisation that are expected to lay the foundation for improved financial performance.

risks.risk: US trade-policy and tariff exposure on India-origin quartz exports
risks.note: Management describes tariff-related uncertainty in the US as, without question, the single most significant external factor affecting performance during the year, particularly in the second half: it compressed realisations, introduced hesitancy into customer ordering patterns and contributed meaningfully to fourth-quarter margin pressure. India segment revenue fell to `748.36 million from `1,419.12 million and the USA segment to `523.43 million from `831.41 million, both attributed to elevated tariffs and evolving trade-policy uncertainty.

risks.risk: Pending QMAA Section 201 global safeguard petition in the United States
risks.note: Foreign-manufactured quartz surface products currently represent approximately 90% of the U.S. market, which led the QMAA to file the Section 201 safeguard petition. The Board's Report calls the potential imposition of a broad-based global safeguard tariff a watershed development for all quartz-exporting nations including India — an unresolved regulatory event that could reset access to the Company's largest market.

risks.risk: Extreme geographic and single-market revenue concentration
risks.note: The USA alone accounted for 77.2% of FY26 revenue and North America (USA and Canada combined) 82.2% of total revenue. Diversification is under way — North America's share fell from an implied 88.8% in FY25 while MENA rose from 7.9% to 13.2% — but the business remains dependent on one policy jurisdiction, and the Company is explicit that it moved deliberately to reduce dependence on any single market.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption in the Middle East and Red Sea region
risks.note: The Board's Report attributes part of the UAE segment loss to geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East and Red Sea region affecting logistics and demand, and the Chairman records approximately 45 days of disruption caused by the regional conflict. This is a direct threat to the shipping routes on which the Jebel Ali-based manufacturing and distribution strategy depends.

risks.risk: Prolonged under-utilisation of installed capacity at both manufacturing units
risks.note: The Dubai (FZE) facility averaged 44% utilisation for the full year against installed capacity of 622,895 sqm per annum, while the Jaipur SEZ unit operated at only 23% average capacity utilisation against installed capacity of 521,450 sqm per annum, reflecting broader demand softness. The UAE segment loss of `(391.76) million is attributed primarily to absorbing full depreciation and finance costs during the ongoing ramp-up and stabilisation phase, so consolidated profitability hinges on utilisation recovering.

risks.risk: Loss-making consolidated operations with widening losses and negative EBITDA
risks.note: The Group recorded a consolidated net loss before tax of `(230.02) million and a net loss after tax of `(318.39) million in FY26, wider than FY25's `(289.00) million, while EBITDA turned negative to INR (113) million from a positive INR 20 million and fourth-quarter EBITDA margin fell to (41.85)%. Consolidated total comprehensive loss was `(328.27) million.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the Bagru unit closure and its still-unplanned disposal
risks.note: The auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to the Board-approved discontinuation of the Bagru Unit (natural stone processing) with effect from March 31, 2026 in view of sustained losses and continued capacity under-utilization, noting that the Board has only accorded in-principle approval for preparation of a plan for disposal of the said unit — the disposal itself is neither planned in detail nor executed.

risks.risk: Pending regulatory approval for the FZE loan-to-equity conversion
risks.note: The auditor's Emphasis of Matter records that the approved conversion of an existing unsecured loan aggregating Rs. 100 Crores / USD 11,120,997 / AED 40,842,200 granted to wholly owned foreign subsidiary Global Surfaces FZE into equity shares on March 18, 2026 remained pending as at March 31, 2026, awaiting requisite approvals/formalities with the Jebel Ali Free Zone Authority (JAFZA), Dubai.

risks.risk: Standalone profitability dependent on intra-group income rather than trading operations
risks.note: Standalone total income of `1,122.29 million for FY26 included other income of `373.93 million, described as principally attributable to management fees, foreign exchange gains and reimbursements received from subsidiaries as part of intra-group arrangements integral to the multi-shore operating model — while those same subsidiaries were loss-making. The India segment result is likewise credited to a higher contribution from other income including intra-group management fees and reimbursements, a quality-of-earnings and related-party dependency risk.

risks.risk: Deteriorating demand in the core export end-market despite intact long-term structural drivers
risks.note: The Board's Report states that while structural demand drivers — construction activity, home renovation trends and increasing preference for durable, low-maintenance surfaces — remain broadly intact, the near-term environment for Indian quartz exporters has been significantly impacted by evolving trade policies in the United States, and the Chairman notes that softening global trade growth restrained capital expenditure planning across a wide range of industries, including ours.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Global Surfaces Limited, established in 1991, is an integrated Indian manufacturer and exporter of engineered quartz and natural stone surfaces operating a multi-shore model across Jaipur (SEZ) and Jebel Ali Free Zone, Dubai, with roughly 95% of revenue from exports.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company mines, processes, manufactures and supplies premium surface solutions, including engineered quartz, granite, marble and soft quartzite, in slabs and customized countertop applications. It sells largely to international markets serving residential, commercial, hospitality and institutional construction, architecture and interior design projects. Distribution in North America runs through wholly owned subsidiaries Global Surfaces Inc. and Superior Surfaces Inc., while manufacturing and MENA/Europe/Africa distribution is anchored by the wholly owned Dubai subsidiary Global Surfaces FZE.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The global engineered quartz industry, estimated at US$14.83 billion in 2025, is expected to reach US$28.07 billion by 2034 at a CAGR of 7.2%
- The Indian engineered quartz market, valued at approximately US$889.6 million in 2025, is expected to outpace the global rate, growing at 7.6% to reach US$1,579.6 million by 2033
- India's countertop industry, valued at USD 12,846.9 million in 2025, is projected to nearly double to USD 25,071.0 million by 2033, growing at 8.7% annually, driven by urbanisation, organised housing growth and a consumer shift towards branded, premium surfacing solutions
- The global quartz market was valued at approximately USD 8.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 12.7 billion by 2034 at a CAGR of approximately 4.7%, with structural demand drivers - construction activity, home renovation trends and increasing preference for durable, low-maintenance surfaces - remaining broadly intact
- US tariff uncertainty is management's single most significant external factor: it compressed realisations, introduced hesitancy into customer ordering patterns and contributed meaningfully to fourth-quarter margin pressure; the USA accounted for 77.2% of FY26 revenue
- Foreign-manufactured quartz surface products represent approximately 90% of the U.S. market, prompting the QMAA Section 201 safeguard petition; a broad-based global safeguard tariff would be a watershed development for all quartz-exporting nations including India
- Geopolitical disruption in the Middle East and Red Sea region affected logistics and demand, including roughly 45 days of disruption at the Dubai facility
- Operating leverage lever: the Dubai facility ran at 44% average utilisation for the year with a 66% peak in November 2025 against installed capacity of 622,895 sqm p.a., while the Jaipur SEZ unit averaged 23% against 521,450 sqm p.a. - management expects improved utilisation to drive performance
- The UAE segment loss is attributed primarily to continued absorption of full depreciation and finance costs on the new facility during the ongoing ramp-up and stabilisation phase
- Mix shift toward engineered stones, now 94.3% of revenue, which grew from INR 1,950 million to INR 2,200 million, with natural stones consciously wound down
- India's domestic economy offered a comparatively stable and strengthening base, underpinned by logistics upgrades, digital infrastructure expansion, urbanisation and a shift towards higher-value manufacturing

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Dual-shore / multi-shore manufacturing across the Jaipur SEZ unit and the Dubai (FZE) facility, used deliberately to reroute production and export flows in response to tariff and trade-policy shocks and to mitigate region-specific risk
- Reduce dependence on any single market by diversifying geographically: North America's revenue share fell from an implied 88.8% in FY25 to 82.2% in FY26 while MENA rose from 7.9% to 13.2%, Canada from 0.11% to 5.0% and India's domestic contribution from 3.25% to 4.6%
- Pivot the India business to a focused, engineered quartz-led operation by discontinuing the loss-making Bagru natural stone processing unit effective March 31, 2026, entering FY 2026-27 as a leaner manufacturer with a sharpened emphasis on high-value engineered quartz products
- Differentiate through proprietary product technology - Marquartz under an exclusive licence from SQIP, LLC covering MENA with First Right of Refusal in India, patented Non-Push-Up Vein and Push-Up Vein Technology plus proprietary RIFT VEIN and CONVERGENCE technologies, and over 20 utility patents secured across the platform in the past seven years
- Lead on low-silica product safety by developing engineered quartz surfaces with less than 1% crystalline silica content using premium Cristobalite, positioned as a proactive response to tightening global regulation on respirable crystalline silica
- Technology-led manufacturing: sustained investment in automation and digitalisation including CNC automation, rubber-mould press technology, Italian BRETON and German KEDA machinery, SAP ERP and a phased barcode-based inventory tracking rollout
- Cost and working-capital discipline as an explicit management priority - reduced slab thickness, new testing protocols, pre-scheduled production planning, Cristobalite sourcing strategy, and a working capital day reduction from 157 to 71
- Fund working capital growth with short-term borrowings while continuing to reduce long-term leverage
- Strengthen subsidiary capital structure, evidenced by the loan-to-equity conversion at Global Surfaces FZE
- Deepen premium, specification-led project positioning with developers and architects, building on acceptance in projects such as Dubai Mall and Emaar St. Regis and relationships with Damac and Sobha

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Multi-shore manufacturing across India and the UAE lets the Company redirect production and export flows between plants in response to trade-policy shocks, with the Dubai facility providing meaningful potential tariff advantages in the context of the evolving U.S. trade environment
- Exclusive licensing rights from SQIP, LLC to manufacture Marquartz, a patented engineered quartz product, across the MENA region with a First Right of Refusal for India, backed by over 20 utility patents secured across the platform in the past seven years plus proprietary RIFT VEIN and CONVERGENCE technologies
- Early mover in engineered quartz surfaces with less than 1% crystalline silica content using premium Cristobalite, a proactive response to tightening global regulation on respirable crystalline silica following measures such as Australia's 2024 prohibition
- Location advantages: SEZ status in Jaipur and Free Trade Zone status in Dubai give tax incentives, simplified regulatory processes and export competitiveness, with proximity to Jebel Ali Port enabling faster delivery and lower freight costs
- Advanced process technology base including CNC automation, rubber-mould press technology and Italian BRETON and German KEDA machinery, plus SAP ERP and a phased barcode-based inventory tracking rollout
- In-house Research & Development centre at the SEZ unit driving new design development, process optimisation and quality enhancement
- Reference credentials in premium projects including Dubai Mall and Emaar St. Regis, alongside new developer relationships with Damac and Sobha in the Middle East

- Geopolitical disruption in the Middle East and Red Sea region — The Board's Report attributes part of the UAE segment loss to geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East and Red Sea region affecting logistics and demand, and the Chairman records approximately 45 days of disruption caused by the regional conflict. This is a direct threat to the shipping routes on which the Jebel Ali-based manufacturing and distribution strategy depends.
- Prolonged under-utilisation of installed capacity at both manufacturing units — The Dubai (FZE) facility averaged 44% utilisation for the full year against installed capacity of 622,895 sqm per annum, while the Jaipur SEZ unit operated at only 23% average capacity utilisation against installed capacity of 521,450 sqm per annum, reflecting broader demand softness. The UAE segment loss of `(391.76) million is attributed primarily to absorbing full depreciation and finance costs during the ongoing ramp-up and stabilisation phase, so consolidated profitability hinges on utilisation recovering.
- Loss-making consolidated operations with widening losses and negative EBITDA — The Group recorded a consolidated net loss before tax of `(230.02) million and a net loss after tax of `(318.39) million in FY26, wider than FY25's `(289.00) million, while EBITDA turned negative to INR (113) million from a positive INR 20 million and fourth-quarter EBITDA margin fell to (41.85)%. Consolidated total comprehensive loss was `(328.27) million.
- Execution risk on the Bagru unit closure and its still-unplanned disposal — The auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to the Board-approved discontinuation of the Bagru Unit (natural stone processing) with effect from March 31, 2026 in view of sustained losses and continued capacity under-utilization, noting that the Board has only accorded in-principle approval for preparation of a plan for disposal of the said unit — the disposal itself is neither planned in detail nor executed.
- Pending regulatory approval for the FZE loan-to-equity conversion — The auditor's Emphasis of Matter records that the approved conversion of an existing unsecured loan aggregating Rs. 100 Crores / USD 11,120,997 / AED 40,842,200 granted to wholly owned foreign subsidiary Global Surfaces FZE into equity shares on March 18, 2026 remained pending as at March 31, 2026, awaiting requisite approvals/formalities with the Jebel Ali Free Zone Authority (JAFZA), Dubai.
- Standalone profitability dependent on intra-group income rather than trading operations — Standalone total income of `1,122.29 million for FY26 included other income of `373.93 million, described as principally attributable to management fees, foreign exchange gains and reimbursements received from subsidiaries as part of intra-group arrangements integral to the multi-shore operating model — while those same subsidiaries were loss-making. The India segment result is likewise credited to a higher contribution from other income including intra-group management fees and reimbursements, a quality-of-earnings and related-party dependency risk.
- Deteriorating demand in the core export end-market despite intact long-term structural drivers — The Board's Report states that while structural demand drivers — construction activity, home renovation trends and increasing preference for durable, low-maintenance surfaces — remain broadly intact, the near-term environment for Indian quartz exporters has been significantly impacted by evolving trade policies in the United States, and the Chairman notes that softening global trade growth restrained capital expenditure planning across a wide range of industries, including ours.
